title: Trim a Binary Search Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- recursion call-stack depth: up to h (O(n) for a skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced) → O(h)
- no containers/arrays allocated → O(1) extra besides the stack
- not counted: input tree, returned tree (modified in place)
approach: Use the BST property: for any node, all values in its left subtree are smaller and all in its right subtree are larger. So if a node's value is below `low`, the node and its entire left subtree are out of range - only the right subtree can still hold valid values, so recurse there. Symmetrically, if a node's value is above `high`, recurse only on its left subtree. When the node is in range, recursively trim both children in place and keep the node. Each node is visited once.
hints: When a node's value is below `low`, which of its two subtrees could still contain values inside `[low, high]`? The BST ordering property is what lets you decide.
Use recursive depth-first traversal. At node `0` in Example 2 (`val=0 < low=1`), discard it and its left subtree, recurse only on its right child (node `2`).

**Single node out of range** - root value outside `[low, high]` with no children.
`Input: root = [5], low = 1, high = 3` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: returning `root` whenever it is non-null instead of recursing → returns `[5]`

**Root below low, right subtree in range** - root must be replaced by its trimmed right subtree.
`Input: root = [1,null,2], low = 2, high = 3` → `Expected: [2]`
⚠️ Bug: assigning `root->left = trim(...)` and `root->right = trim(...)` then returning `root` even when `val < low` → returns `[1,null,2]`

**Root above high, left subtree contains out-of-range nodes** - returning the raw left child leaves invalid values in the result.
`Input: root = [3,0,null,null,2,null,1], low = 1, high = 2` → `Expected: [2,1]`
⚠️ Bug: returning `root->left` without recursively trimming it when `val > high` → returns `[0,null,2,null,1]`

**Skewed right chain all above high** - entire tree must collapse to null.
`Input: root = [1,null,2,null,3], low = 5, high = 6` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: only checking the root once and not recursing on the appropriate child → returns `[1,null,2,null,3]`

followUps.q: What if the tree is extremely skewed (height ≈ n) and you must avoid recursion-stack overflow?
followUps.a: Convert the recursion to an explicit stack-based DFS, or first rotate the tree to balance it before trimming. Time stays O(n); auxiliary stack space is still O(h) but you control it explicitly and can switch to an iterative Morris-style traversal for O(1) extra space.

followUps.q: What if values are not unique (the BST may contain duplicates)?
followUps.a: The same pruning logic still works because the BST property still orders subtrees; you only need to decide consistently which side equal values live on. Complexity remains O(n) time and O(h) space.

followUps.q: What if the tree is provided as a read-only structure and you must return a brand-new trimmed tree?
followUps.a: Allocate new `TreeNode` objects for every kept node instead of relinking in place; discard out-of-range subtrees without copying them. Time stays O(n); space becomes O(n) for the new tree plus O(h) recursion stack.
